summary: Raman alone does not show that flake 2 is a monolayer. It does show that flake 2 is much thinner than flake 1. The hBN E2g band is weak but real (SNR ≈ 14, about 2700σ in Δχ²). It is about 10× weaker in integrated area than on flake 1. It sits 2.8 cm⁻¹ higher (1369.0 vs 1366.2 cm⁻¹) and is slightly broader (22 vs 18 cm⁻¹). The Si 520 cm⁻¹ line is about 19× stronger than on flake 1. All of this fits a very thin flake, but a thin few-layer flake gives the same signature, and the upshift can also come from strain or substrate effects. Monolayer vs. a few layers needs AFM, optical contrast calibrated against known layers, or low-frequency layer-breathing/shear modes, which are not in this window (450–1650 cm⁻¹).

observations.finding: Both flakes show the hBN E2g mode near 1366–1369 cm⁻¹. Flake 2 is a genuine weak signal, not noise or a cosmic ray.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits, 1300–1440 cm⁻¹. Flake 1: 1366.19±0.04 cm⁻¹, FWHM 17.9±0.13, amplitude ≈3230 counts above background, SNR ≈ 80 (residual σ ≈ 40). Flake 2: 1368.97±0.24 cm⁻¹, FWHM 22.5±0.9, amplitude ≈ 271 counts, SNR ≈ 14 (σ ≈ 19), Δχ² vs a flat baseline ≈ 2700σ². The band is broad and Lorentzian, with no D/G carbon bands in either spectrum (nothing above noise at ~1580 cm⁻¹ in flake 2), so it is not amorphous-carbon contamination.

observations.finding: The E2g intensity on flake 2 is about 10% of that on flake 1. If the signal scales roughly linearly with layer number, flake 2 is about 10× thinner than flake 1, which is a ratio and not an absolute thickness.
observations.evidence: Integrated areas (π/2·A·FWHM): flake 1 ≈ 9.1×10⁴, flake 2 ≈ 9.5×10³, ratio ≈ 0.105 (amplitude ratio 0.084). Flake 2 is a monolayer only if flake 1 is about ≤10 layers (≈3 nm). A 30 nm flake 1 (~90 layers) would put flake 2 near 9 layers. Flake 1's thickness is not given.

observations.finding: The Si 520.9 cm⁻¹ line is about 19× stronger on flake 2 than on flake 1. This is the expected direction for thinner flake 2, but it is a weak thickness metric.
observations.evidence: Si amplitude ≈ 18,000 counts (flake 2, FWHM 3.50 cm⁻¹) vs ≈ 980 counts (flake 1, FWHM 3.37 cm⁻¹). The Si second-order band at ~940–980 cm⁻¹ is visible on flake 2 (≈630 counts above baseline) but not on flake 1. Thin hBN is transparent, so a 19× Si drop on flake 1 is more than I would expect from absorption. It likely also reflects interference in the 290 nm SiO2 stack, focus/collection differences and scattering from the thicker flake, so I would not use it to count layers.

observations.finding: The E2g band on flake 2 is upshifted by about +2.8 cm⁻¹ and broadened relative to flake 1. This is the qualitative trend reported for thinning toward a monolayer, but it is not specific to a monolayer.
observations.evidence: Δν = +2.78±0.25 cm⁻¹ (flake 2 minus flake 1). Δ FWHM = +4.5±0.9 cm⁻¹. Flake 1 at 1366.2 cm⁻¹ is bulk-like. The shift is larger than the fit error but smaller than the range from strain, substrate coupling or adsorbates. The FWHM difference is only ~5σ at SNR 14, and baseline choice moves it by about 1 cm⁻¹.
observations.source: Gorbachev et al., Small 7, 465 (2011), 'Hunting for monolayer boron nitride', Raman section. Recalled from memory: bulk ≈1366 cm⁻¹, monolayer a few cm⁻¹ higher, intensity roughly linear in layer number. Please verify exact values.

observations.finding: Flake 1 is much broader than good bulk hBN, whose E2g FWHM is typically below ~10 cm⁻¹ at 295 K.
observations.evidence: FWHM 17.9 cm⁻¹ with a fixed 8 cm⁻¹ width fit rejected (χ²/σ² 11,042 vs 179). The Si line is only 3.4 cm⁻¹ wide, so instrumental broadening cannot explain it. Possible causes are low crystal quality, strain gradients, or isotopic/impurity content of the source crystal. Flake 2's width (22 cm⁻¹) is therefore not an independent monolayer indicator, because the reference bulk width is already large.
observations.source: Bulk hBN E2g reference: Nemanich, Solin & Guerard, Phys. Rev. B 23, 6348 (1981); Reich et al., Phys. Rev. B 71, 205201 (2005). Typical linewidths recalled from memory.

observations.finding: Flake 1 has a sloping background (~450→1150 counts from 450 to 1250 cm⁻¹) that flake 2 does not have (flat ≈1600–1750 counts).
observations.evidence: Background slope about +1 count/cm⁻¹ on flake 1 vs about 0.1 (≈ flat) on flake 2.

properties.name: layers
properties.value: not determined; thin (probably few-layer to monolayer). Monolayer is possible but not demonstrated. Flake 2 is about 10× thinner than flake 1 if the signal scales linearly.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: Not assessable for flake 2 (SNR too low). Flake 1 linewidth is broad (17.9 cm⁻¹), which suggests medium disorder or a poor-quality source crystal.

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: Cannot be separated from thickness effects. The +2.8 cm⁻¹ shift would be tensile-looking only if the thickness trend is excluded.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: none determinable (hBN E2g is insensitive to doping)

caveats: Absolute layer number needs an intensity calibration (AFM height, or known 1L/2L/3L flakes on the same substrate). The linear scaling with layer number is only approximate on 290 nm SiO2, where interference and focus change the signal.

Intensity ratios depend on focus and on the Si/SiO2 interference. Flake 1 and flake 2 have very different Si 520 signals (19×), so focus, collection or local stack differences could bias the ~10× area ratio by a large factor.

The +2.8 cm⁻¹ upshift can also arise from strain, substrate pinning, adsorbates or a different thin-layer count (2–5 layers). The 2.8 cm⁻¹ difference is only ~11× the fit error, and flake 1 and flake 2 may come from different crystals or differently strained regions. Wavenumber calibration drift between acquisitions is also possible, but the Si line sits at 520.9 cm⁻¹ in both, so calibration looks consistent to about 0.03 cm⁻¹.
The flake 2 linewidth (22.5±0.9 cm⁻¹) depends on baseline choice and SNR, so the broadening relative to flake 1 should not be over-interpreted.

The spectral window (450–1650 cm⁻¹) excludes the low-frequency interlayer shear and breathing modes (a few tens of cm⁻¹) that distinguish 2L, 3L and so on. They are absent for a monolayer, so they would settle the question.
Optical visibility alone is not diagnostic: a faint flake on 290 nm SiO2 only means it is thin (few nm or less), and 1L vs 3L vs 5L all have low contrast.

hBN at 514.5 nm is a non-resonant, below-gap measurement, so there is no resonance enhancement. The monolayer signal is intrinsically very weak, and a flake showing SNR 14 at the same integration time as flake 1 is a little strong for a pure monolayer, though that is only a qualitative remark.
questions_for_user: What is the AFM thickness (or optical contrast) of flake 1 and flake 2? This is the only way to convert the ≈10× intensity ratio to layer numbers.

What are the spectrometer grating and resolution, and are the flake 2 data a single spot or an average? Several spots, plus a map across the flake, would show whether the ~1369 cm⁻¹ position and the intensity are uniform or vary with local thickness steps.
Were the focus and laser power identical for both flakes? The Si intensity differs 19×, so refocusing may have been done. What was the power, and is there any sign of heating or drift?
Do you have a low-frequency spectrum (below ~100 cm⁻¹) with an ultra-low-frequency filter? Interlayer shear/breathing modes would give a direct layer-number count for flake 2.

What is the source of the hBN crystal and the exfoliation method (tape residue, PDMS)? The broad 17.9 cm⁻¹ line on flake 1 and the sloping background could come from the crystal or from contamination.
Is the flake on the same SiO2 thickness (290 nm) everywhere, and was the Raman mapped relative to a bare-Si reference spectrum on the same day? That would allow Si-normalised intensities.

limits: Raman at 514.5 nm and the window covered cannot give a unique layer count, and cannot by itself separate a monolayer from a few-layer flake of ~2–10 layers.
The data cannot tell crystal quality or strain on flake 2 at this SNR.
The data cannot tell doping, magnetic order or temperature effects (one temperature, 295 K; hBN is non-magnetic and E2g is insensitive to doping).
Absolute thickness of either flake is not constrained without a calibration standard or AFM; only the ≈10× ratio is measured, and it is uncertain by the focus/interference effects above.
No two-point or mapping information is available, so uniformity of flake 2 is unknown.
